2026-04-26.text:
Overcast skies softened the light as we wound through volcanic breccia corridors at Pinnacles after scrapping the coastal drive when CA-1 was closed for the Big Sur Marathon. The inland detour on CA-101 turned out to be the better call.

**Highlights:**
- [Pinnacles National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinnacles_National_Park) — formed from the eroded remnants of an ancient volcano that migrated ~195 miles north along the San Andreas Fault; one of the few recovery sites for the reintroduced California condor, with resident birds regularly spotted soaring above the crags.

2026-04-27.text:
Morning started among the vines outside Paso Robles before we headed south to hike the open space hills above San Luis Obispo, surprising a garter snake sunning itself on the trail mid-afternoon.

**Highlights:**

- [Paso Robles Wine Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paso_Robles_wine_country) — AVA straddling the Templeton Gap, where a dramatic day-to-night temperature swing of up to 50°F is credited for producing unusually structured Rhône-style reds.
- [San Luis Obispo Open Space Trails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Luis_Obispo,_California) — the city preserves over 14,000 acres of open space, with trails offering direct views of the downtown basin and Santa Lucia Range from volcanic-soil hillsides.
- [Common Garter Snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_garter_snake) — one of North America's most cold-tolerant snakes, capable of surviving brief freezing by producing cryoprotectant compounds in its blood.

2026-04-28.text:
Morro Rock filled the frame as we pushed off from the bay's pebbly shore mid-morning, two kayakers in a red tandem threading past channel markers below the 581-foot volcanic plug. By noon we'd driven south to Montaña de Oro, hiking the bluff trail past tilted Monterey shale fins and sheltered coves before resting against a folded cliff face for a group selfie.

**Highlights:**
- [Morro Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morro_Rock) — one of the Nine Sisters volcanic chain, it serves as a nesting sanctuary for peregrine falcons and public climbing has been banned since 1968.
- [Montaña de Oro State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montaña_de_Oro_State_Park) — its name means "Mountain of Gold," referencing the wildflowers that blanket its marine terraces each spring.

2026-04-29.text:
Early morning cottontails outside a Pismo Beach fence gave way to a sunny bike ride out to Avila Beach's pier, then an afternoon exploring sea arches and tide pools back along the coast.

**Highlights:**

- [Avila Beach Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avila_Beach,_California) — a sheltered cove pier backed by steep coastal bluffs, serving both recreational cyclists and small commercial fishing vessels registered out of the area
- [Dinosaur Caves Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_Caves_Park) — a Pismo Beach clifftop park named for a now-demolished roadside attraction that once housed a life-size dinosaur; its sandstone headland exposes tide pools at low water
- [Pismo Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pismo_Beach,_California) — the rocky coastline here contains wave-carved sea arches accessible at low tide, a product of differential erosion in the Monterey Formation sandstone
